backlog.spec: Supply jac for the objective (-1 on radii, 0 on centres) and an analytic constraint Jacobian (pair distance, wall, and radius-positivity rows) to minimize. This removes finite-difference cost (about 130 evals per gradient) and gives many more restarts and iterations in 24 s. Build the Jacobian with numpy indexing using the precomputed iu pairs.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the sqrt pair constraint with the smooth form (dx^2+dy^2) - (ri+rj)^2 >= 0, together with ri+rj>=0 implied by r>=0. Use the analytic Jacobian. This avoids the sqrt singularity and makes the constraints polynomial.
backlog.title: Squared-distance constraints

backlog.spec: Set MAX_ITER=1000 and add ftol=1e-12 to the SLSQP options so that each run converges fully. Combine with analytic Jacobians if possible. Fewer but fully converged runs usually give better local optima than truncated ones.
backlog.title: Raise MAX_ITER to 1000

backlog.spec: Run many short SLSQP runs (maxiter 60). Keep the top 3 by sum of radii after repair. Then continue each with maxiter 500 and ftol 1e-13 starting from the result. Return the best.
backlog.title: Two-stage: fast screen, then polish

backlog.spec: After about 40% of the time, switch to perturbation search. Take the best (c,r), add Gaussian noise (sd about 0.03) to the centres, set radii to 0.8 of their values, re-run SLSQP, and accept if better. Repeat until the time is used.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the best

backlog.spec: Start each run from a jittered lattice, e.g. a 5x5 grid plus one extra circle, or a random choice of rows such as 5,5,6,5,5. Jitter sd is about 0.02 and the initial radius is 0.08. Known good packings are near hex or grid structures, so this beats uniform random starts.
backlog.title: Grid-based initialisation

backlog.spec: Initialise with rows of circles with counts randomly chosen from the partitions of 26 into 5 or 6 rows (e.g. 5,5,5,5,6). Space the rows evenly, offset alternate rows, and add small noise. Then run SLSQP.
backlog.title: Row-structured hex starts

backlog.spec: Set TIME_FRACTION=0.92. The repair is cheap. Guard it by estimating the duration of the last restart and stopping if the next restart is likely to exceed the 30 s limit. Gives more restarts.
backlog.title: Increase TIME_FRACTION to 0.92

backlog.spec: Set INIT_RADIUS to 0.03 and INIT_LOW to 0.05 so that the starts are not overlapping so much. Test whether the more feasible starts converge to better optima.
backlog.title: Smaller initial radii

backlog.spec: Draw initial radii uniformly in [0.02,0.12] instead of a constant. This diversifies the sizes of the circles (large and small mixes are optimal here).
backlog.title: Random initial radii

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, fix the centres and solve an LP with scipy.optimize.linprog to maximise sum r subject to ri+rj<=dij, r<=wall distance, r>=0. Then subtract 1e-12 and verify. This recovers the slack lost by the greedy repair.
backlog.title: Better repair via exact LP

backlog.spec: Iterate: fix the centres and solve the LP for radii; then do an SLSQP step on the centres and radii with few iterations. Repeat 3 times on the top candidates. This polishes each candidate to a vertex solution.
backlog.title: Alternate LP radii and centre steps

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, do 100 steps of gradient descent on the overlap penalty with growing radii (L-BFGS-B with analytic gradient), so that SLSQP starts from a near-feasible state. This reduces the failed runs.
backlog.title: Penalty-based pre-relaxation

backlog.spec: Set SHRINK=1e-11 (the tolerance is 1e-10). After the repair, verify validity with the exact check and increase the shrink only if needed. Gains about 1e-8 per circle, tiny but free.
backlog.title: Tighter repair shrink

backlog.spec: From the best solution, remove the smallest circle and place it at a random point (or the largest hole found by sampling 2000 points and choosing the one with the maximum clearance). Then re-run SLSQP. Accept if improved. Use for the last 50% of the time.
backlog.title: Drop and reinsert smallest circle

backlog.spec: From the best solution, swap the positions of a large circle and a small circle (keep radii attached to the new places), and re-optimise with SLSQP at maxiter 200. Accept if better.
backlog.title: Swap-size perturbation

backlog.spec: Initialise with the centres symmetric about the diagonal or the vertical axis (13 mirrored pairs). Optimise in full space from there. Symmetric optima are common in packings.
backlog.title: Symmetric starts

backlog.spec: Include only constraints for pairs with distance less than 0.45 at the start of each SLSQP run, and re-check validity after. Solve again with all pairs if violated. This reduces the cost per iteration (325 pairs down to about 100).
backlog.title: Active-pair constraint pruning

backlog.spec: Take the best SLSQP result and polish it with scipy trust-constr using the analytic Jacobian, or SLSQP with ftol=1e-15 and maxiter 1000. Use the last 10% of the time for this.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish

backlog.spec: Place 12 to 14 circles near the walls (random along the perimeter at distance about 0.08) and the rest inside. The best packings have many circles touching the walls.
backlog.title: Boundary-biased starts

backlog.spec: Draw the centres by a stratified sample (scipy.stats.qmc.LatinHypercube or Sobol seeded by rng) in place of uniform. More even coverage means fewer clumped starts.
backlog.title: Latin-hypercube starts

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP at maxiter 40 and abandon the restart if the sum of radii is under 2.55. Otherwise continue with maxiter 400. Saves time on bad basins.
backlog.title: Reject bad starts early

backlog.spec: Precompute iu and avoid reconstructing arrays in cons. Use np.hypot and preallocated output. Reduces overhead per eval, so more restarts occur.
backlog.title: Vectorised constraint speed-up

backlog.spec: First solve with a constraint r<=0.12 and the same sum objective, then release the cap and continue from that result. This regularises the early phase and avoids a few huge circles.
backlog.title: Soft-start with a radius cap

backlog.spec: First minimise -sum(r) plus 0.1*sum of squares of r (encouraging equal radii) for 100 iterations. Then use the pure objective. Smooths the landscape.
backlog.title: Weighted objective warm start

backlog.spec: Keep the top 5 solutions. To create a new start, take the left half (x<0.5) circles from one elite and the right half from another, fill to 26 circles by adding or removing random ones, then optimise.
backlog.title: Keep an elite pool and recombine

backlog.spec: Take the best solution, multiply the radii by 0.5 and add centre noise of sd 0.01, then re-run SLSQP. Cycle with noise sd chosen randomly from {0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05}.
backlog.title: Perturb with radius shrink then regrow

backlog.spec: Use the start from a 5x5 grid (radius 0.1) with the 26th circle placed at a random gap corner, plus noise 0.01. Run SLSQP with a large maxiter. Test as a structured start for 30% of the restarts.
backlog.title: Seed with 5x5 plus one in the gap

backlog.spec: After the repair, compute the max overlap and wall violation in double precision. If any exceed 0, shrink by the violation plus 1e-12 until valid. Prevents crashes when other aggressive changes make the repair less safe.
backlog.title: Final exact validation loop

backlog.spec: If finite differences are retained, set options eps=1e-8 so that the gradients are more accurate. Also test ftol=1e-10. Cheap hyperparameter change.
backlog.title: Use SLSQP eps tuning

backlog.spec: Provide an analytic Jacobian for SLSQP via the jac argument of minimize and for the constraints. Objective gradient: zeros for centres, -1 for radii. Constraint Jacobian: dense matrix of shape (m, 3n), built with precomputed index arrays iu. For pair k=(i,j): d/dci = (ci-cj)/dist, d/dcj = -(ci-cj)/dist, d/dri = d/drj = -1. Wall constraints have +-1 entries on the centre coordinate and -1 on the radius, and the r>=0 rows have +1. This should make each SLSQP iteration much cheaper, so more restarts and perturbation cycles fit in 30 s. Keep the rest of the code (30% restarts, then perturbation) unchanged.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobian plus replicate of perturb scheme

backlog.spec: After the 30% random-restart phase, loop: perturb the current best (centres + normal noise of sd chosen from [0.01,0.03,0.06], radii x0.5), run SLSQP, repair, and replace best only if the sum improves. Additionally, on each iteration with probability 0.3 perturb only a random cluster: pick one random circle and its 5 nearest neighbours, resample just those centres uniformly in their bounding region, and leave the others fixed. Use the result as the start for SLSQP with all radii x0.5.
backlog.title: Repeated perturb-and-reoptimise basin hopping with acceptance

backlog.spec: Keep the top 5 packings found by the random-restart phase, sorted by sum of radii. In the perturbation phase, pick a pool member at random each cycle (weighted toward the best), perturb it, re-optimise, and insert the result into the pool if it beats the worst member and differs from all members by more than 1e-4 in sum of radii. Return the best of the pool. This avoids tunnelling into one basin.
backlog.title: Elite pool with distinct local optima

backlog.spec: For random restarts, run SLSQP with maxiter=40. Keep the result only if its sum of radii after a quick clip is within 0.03 of the best so far. Otherwise discard it. Promising candidates are polished with a second SLSQP run for maxiter=300 started from the screen result. This spends most of the time on promising basins and allows roughly 3x more starts.
backlog.title: Two-stage SLSQP: short screen then polish

backlog.spec: Make a fraction (50%) of the random starts as follows: place 25 circles on a jittered 5x5 grid with spacing 0.2 (jitter sd 0.02, centres at 0.1+0.2*k) and place the 26th circle at a random point. Set all radii to 0.08. Other starts stay uniform random. Also use some starts with a 5-5-6-5-5 row layout, with each row evenly spaced and jittered. The best known packings are near-hex with irregular rows, so these starts are near good basins.
backlog.title: Structured start: 5x5 grid plus one extra circle

backlog.spec: Instead of the constant INIT_RADIUS of 0.05, draw the initial radii uniformly from [0.03, 0.12] per circle in random starts. This favours the mixed large/small radius structure of the best packing and gives diverse topologies. Use the same SLSQP settings.
backlog.title: Random initial radii with varying sizes

backlog.spec: At the end of the time budget (reserve the last 10%), take the best packing, run SLSQP from it (radii not halved) with ftol=1e-15 and maxiter=500, then repair with SHRINK=1e-12 rather than 1e-9. Accept only if the repaired sum is larger and the packing is valid. This recovers the small amounts lost to SLSQP stopping early and to the repair shrinkage.
backlog.title: Final high-precision polish with LP-free tight SLSQP

backlog.spec: Reformulate the pair constraints as smooth squared distance: (dx^2+dy^2) - (ri+rj)^2 >= 0, together with the constraint ri+rj >= 0 implied by r>=0. Provide the analytic Jacobian. This removes the sqrt non-smoothness at coincident centres and gives better conditioning in SLSQP. The repair step stays the same, so validity is guaranteed.
backlog.title: Squared-distance constraints with analytic Jacobian

backlog.spec: In SLSQP, only include pair constraints for pairs whose centre distance in the start point is less than 0.45. A circle of radius up to about 0.2 can never touch a far-away circle. After the solve, check all pairs. If any are violated, re-solve with the full constraint set, warm-started from the result. This cuts the constraint count from 325 to roughly 100 and speeds up each SLSQP iteration, since its cost is cubic in the number of constraints.
backlog.title: Active-set constraint pruning

backlog.spec: Run each random start in two phases. In phase 1, add the bound r_i <= 0.11 and run SLSQP for 60 iterations. This regularises toward equal-size packings and gets the layout. In phase 2, remove the cap (bounds 0 to 0.5) and continue from the phase-1 result for up to 200 iterations. The aim is to improve the quality of local optima compared with a single-stage solve.
backlog.title: Soft radius cap annealing

backlog.spec: In solve(), change the threshold for switching from random restarts to perturbation of the best packing from 0.3 * time_limit to 0.2 * time_limit. Nothing else changes. This tests whether more time spent perturbing the incumbent helps.
backlog.title: Replicate slot 2 with 20% restart phase

backlog.spec: After 30% of the time, keep a current packing (c, r). Each iteration perturbs the current packing: centres get Gaussian noise with sd drawn from [0.01, 0.02, 0.05], and radii are scaled by 0.5. Re-optimise with SLSQP and repair. Accept as the new current if the sum of radii is greater than current sum minus 0.003. Track the global best separately and return it. Reset current to best every 10 iterations that fail to improve.
backlog.title: Basin hopping with acceptance and decaying sd

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, do not perturb all circles. Pick a random centre point in the square and select the 6-8 circles nearest to it. Re-draw their centres uniformly inside a disc of radius 0.2 around that point and set their radii to 0.03. Leave the other circles at their best-packing positions, with radii x0.7. Run SLSQP and repair. Keep the result if it is better than the best.
backlog.title: Local perturbation of a subset of circles

backlog.spec: Reserve the last 10% of the time. Run SLSQP on the best packing from its own centres and radii, with maxiter=1000 and ftol=1e-15. Repair it with SHRINK=1e-12 and keep the result only if the repaired sum of radii is larger than the best. Check the validity with the exact pairwise test before accepting it.
backlog.title: Final tight polish of best packing

backlog.spec: Make a fraction of the restarts (every second one) start from a 5x5 grid of centres at spacing 0.2 with offset 0.1, plus a 26th circle at a random position. Add Gaussian noise of sd 0.03 to all centres. Set initial radii to 0.08 for the grid circles and 0.03 for the extra one. Other restarts remain uniform random.
backlog.title: 5x5 grid plus one start

backlog.spec: For random restarts, draw the initial radii from uniform(0.02, 0.12) instead of the constant 0.05. This diversifies the size distribution in the local optima, and the large radii are placed at the corners. Keep everything else the same.
backlog.title: Random initial radii

backlog.spec: Keep the top 5 distinct packings by sum of radii. They count as distinct if their sums differ by more than 1e-4. After 30% of the time, create each child as follows. Take a random vertical or horizontal cut at a coordinate in [0.3, 0.7]. Combine the circles of parent A on one side with those of parent B on the other side. If the count is not 26, drop circles at random or add them at random positions. Set the radii x0.5, run SLSQP and repair, and insert the child in the pool if it is good enough.
backlog.title: Elite pool with recombination

backlog.spec: Run each restart in two stages. Stage 1 adds an upper bound r <= 0.1 (through the bounds argument of minimize) with maxiter 80. Stage 2 removes the cap and continues from the stage 1 result with maxiter 200. The cap pushes the circles to equalise before the large ones grow.
backlog.title: Radius-cap annealed SLSQP

backlog.spec: For each restart, first run 30 SLSQP iterations. Then build the constraint set from the pairs with a gap below 0.15 only (all wall constraints stay) and run SLSQP on that set with maxiter 300. Finally check all pairs in the repair step. This shrinks the constraint count from 325 to about 80 and makes each iteration faster, so more restarts fit in the time.
backlog.title: Active-pair pruning in SLSQP

backlog.spec: For half of the restarts, generate 13 random circles in the left half of the square (x < 0.5) and mirror them to x -> 1 - x, giving 26 circles. Add noise of sd 0.01 to break the exact symmetry. Then run SLSQP as usual. Symmetric local optima are often good for this problem.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric starts

backlog.spec: Keep a pool of the top 5 distinct packings (distinct if the sorted radii vectors differ by more than 1e-3 in max-norm). After 30% of the time, each iteration picks a random pool member, perturbs it (centres + normal sd chosen from [0.01,0.02,0.05], radii x0.5), re-optimises with SLSQP, repairs, and inserts the result into the pool if it is better than the worst member and distinct. Return the best pool member.
backlog.title: Elite pool with distinct optima and perturbation

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase (after 30% of time), instead of jittering all centres, pick a random point in the square and jitter only the 6-8 circles nearest to it with sd 0.05-0.1, leaving the others fixed. Set all radii to 0.5x as in the current scheme. Re-optimise with SLSQP, repair, keep if better than the best.
backlog.title: Perturb only a local subset of circles

backlog.spec: In the second phase, take the best packing, remove the 3 smallest circles and re-place them at random positions (uniform in [0.05,0.95]) with radius 0.03. Scale other radii by 0.8, run SLSQP, repair, accept if better. Differs from the earlier single-circle max-clearance move by using random multi-circle reinsertion.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert the 3 smallest circles at random holes

backlog.spec: For random restarts, add an upper bound on the radii in the constraints (r <= cap) and run SLSQP twice: first with cap=0.11 for 60 iterations, then drop the cap and continue from that solution with MAX_ITER=200. This encourages balanced starting layouts before the free optimisation. Keep the repair step unchanged.
backlog.title: Soft radius cap annealing

backlog.spec: For half of the random restarts, generate 13 random centres in the left half (x in [0.05,0.5]) and mirror them about x=0.5 to produce 26 centres, with a small jitter of 0.01. Use the usual initial radius. Optimise without enforcing symmetry. The other half stay uniform random.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric starts

backlog.spec: Build the pair constraints only for pairs whose centre distance in the starting point is below 0.4, and recompute the pair list after a first 60-iteration SLSQP run, then run a second SLSQP run with the new list (pairs with distance below 0.35). This shrinks the constraint count and speeds up each SLSQP call, allowing more restarts. Validate with _repair at the end, which stays exact.
backlog.title: Active-pair pruning in SLSQP

backlog.spec: After the main loop, take the best packing and run SLSQP again from it with maxiter=500 and ftol=1e-14, with the radii left unshrunk, and then repair. Keep the polished result only if its sum of radii after repair is larger. Reserve the last 8% of the time limit for this.
backlog.title: Final tight polish with active-set Newton-like SLSQP

backlog.spec: Pass bounds to SLSQP: centres in [0,1] and radii in [0,0.5], and remove the r>=0 constraints and the four wall constraints' redundancy only for r. This reduces the constraint count by 26 and can improve convergence. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Trust-constr or SLSQP with bounded variables

backlog.spec: For random restarts, run the first SLSQP stage (40 iterations) with objective -sum(r) + 2*sum(r**2) to discourage large radii concentrated in a few circles and push towards balanced layouts. Then run the true objective -sum(r) for the full MAX_ITER from that point.
backlog.title: Weighted-objective warm start

backlog.spec: In the second phase, perturb the best packing by a structured move: pick a random vertical or horizontal strip of width 0.3, shift the centres of the circles in it by a random offset of up to 0.08 along the strip's length (wrapping with clipping to [0.05,0.95]), set radii x0.5, re-optimise, repair, and keep if better. This explores collective moves that independent jitter cannot.
backlog.title: Perturbation by random-rotation of a row/block

backlog.spec: Change the switch threshold in solve from 0.3 * time_limit to 0.25 * time_limit and keep everything else unchanged. Purpose: a cheap confirmation and tuning of the perturb-best scheme at a different split, to separate real gain from noise.
backlog.title: Replicate slot 2 baseline with 25% restart phase

backlog.spec: After 25% of the time, keep a current packing cur (initially best). Each iteration: perturb cur with centre noise sd drawn from [0.01,0.02,0.03], radii x0.5, re-optimise with SLSQP, repair. Accept as the new cur if its sum is >= cur.sum - 0.002 (small tolerance); update best separately. Reset cur to best if no best improvement for 8 iterations.
backlog.title: Perturb-and-accept chain from current packing

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, take the best packing, pick the k=2-3 smallest circles, and relocate them to random points sampled among 2000 random candidates, choosing those with the largest distance-to-nearest-circle-surface (distance to centres minus radii, and to walls). Set their radii to 0.02, keep the others' radii x0.7, run SLSQP, repair, and keep if better.
backlog.title: Remove and reinsert the 3 smallest circles at largest holes

backlog.spec: After the main loop, run SLSQP on the best packing once more starting from its exact centres and radii (not shrunk), with maxiter=500, ftol=1e-12, and bounds on variables (centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]). Then repair, and keep the result only if the sum is larger than the current best.
backlog.title: Final tight polish with bounded SLSQP

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts, run SLSQP in three stages with an added constraint r_i <= cap, cap = 0.09, 0.12, then none, each stage warm-starting from the previous result, 70 iterations each. The cap keeps circles similar in size early and lets the radii differentiate later. Use via bounds on the radius variables.
backlog.title: Radius-cap annealing within each restart

backlog.spec: Start half of the fresh restarts from a perturbed triangular lattice: rows of 5,5,6,5,5 circles (or 6,5,6,5,4 chosen randomly) with row y spread evenly in [0.1,0.9], x evenly spaced with row offsets, add Gaussian noise sd 0.02 to centres, and set the radii to 0.07. Other restarts remain uniform random.
backlog.title: Hex-like 26-circle seeds with random defect

backlog.spec: Keep the top 4 distinct packings from the restart phase. In the later phase, build a child by choosing a random vertical or horizontal cut line, taking the circles of parent A on one side, and of parent B on the other, adjusting to exactly 26 circles by deleting the smallest or adding random points. Radii x0.5, SLSQP, repair; insert into the pool if good.
backlog.title: Elite crossover by region

backlog.spec: For each fresh start, first run 50 SLSQP iterations maximising sum of w_i*r_i with random weights w_i uniform in [0.5,1.5], then continue with the true objective for up to 200 iterations from that result. The random weights bias which circles grow large, diversifying basins.
backlog.title: Weighted-objective warm start

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, pick a random circle subset (those whose centre lies in a random disc of radius 0.3), rotate their centres about the disc centre by a random angle in [-0.5,0.5] rad or translate them by a random vector of norm 0.05, clip into [0.05,0.95], radii x0.5, re-optimise and repair, keep if better.
backlog.title: Block rotation / shift perturbation

backlog.spec: Set the screening MAX_ITER to 120 for restarts during the first 50% of the time, store all results, then spend the remaining time polishing the top 3 packings (SLSQP from their exact state, maxiter 400) and finally perturbation on the best. Differs from earlier screening by using a pool of 3 and a polish from unshrunk radii.
backlog.title: Smaller MAX_ITER with more restarts, then long polish of top 3

backlog.spec: Change the switch threshold from 0.3*time_limit to 0.25*time_limit. In the perturbation phase, keep the current packing `cur` (initially best) and perturb `cur` instead of `best` each iteration. Accept the new result as `cur` if its sum is >= cur.sum() - 0.002, and update `best` whenever it improves. Keep the remaining settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Replicate slot 2 with 25% restart phase and chained perturbation

backlog.spec: Set SHRINK = 2e-12 (the harness tolerance is 1e-10). After _repair, run one more validation pass that computes the max overlap in double precision. If any pair still overlaps by more than 5e-11, scale the radii by a tiny factor until valid. This should recover about 1e-9 per circle, which is small but free. Keep the code to about 5 lines.
backlog.title: Tighter repair shrink with 1e-12 margin

backlog.spec: Pass bounds to SLSQP: centres in [0,1] and radii in [0,0.5]. Remove the explicit r>=0 constraint block from cons. This shrinks the constraint vector by 26 entries and keeps iterates in range, so restarts may converge better. Leave everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Bounded-variable SLSQP with box bounds

backlog.spec: Keep the top 4 distinct packings from the restart phase. In the perturbation phase, build a child by choosing a random vertical or horizontal cut at a position in 0.3-0.7. Take the circles of parent A with centres on one side and the circles of parent B on the other side. Fill to n circles by dropping the smallest extras or adding circles at random positions with small radii. Then run SLSQP from the child with radii x0.5. Fall back to perturbation of the best if the child is worse than the best.
backlog.title: Elite recombination by region

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts, run a first SLSQP of 60 iterations with the objective -sum(w*r), where w is drawn from uniform(0.5,1.5) per circle with the rng. Then run the standard objective (w=1) for MAX_ITER iterations from that result. The random weights bias which circles get large and diversify the basins.
backlog.title: Weighted-objective warm start

backlog.spec: After the main loop ends at 0.75*time_limit, polish the best packing with scipy trust-constr using the same constraints (analytic sparse Jacobian is not needed; use a finite-difference Jacobian of the 2-point type) for at most 4 s of CPU time (via maxiter and an xtol of 1e-12). Run _repair on the result. Accept it only if the repaired sum is larger than the best.
backlog.title: Trust-constr final polish of the best

backlog.spec: For half of the fresh restarts, build the start from a hexagonal arrangement. Use 5 rows alternating 5 and 6 circles, which gives 27 positions, and drop one random circle. Use spacing about 0.18 with an offset on alternate rows. Add gaussian noise sd 0.02 to the centres, set the radii to 0.08, and clip the centres to [0.05,0.95]. The other half stay uniform random.
backlog.title: Hex-defect starts with 26 circles

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, pick a random line (vertical or horizontal) through the packing at a coordinate in 0.3-0.7. Shift all circles on one side of it by a random vector of magnitude 0.03-0.08 along the line, and clip to [0.05,0.95]. Then halve the radii and run SLSQP. Alternate this with the existing gaussian jitter at 50% probability each.
backlog.title: Block shift perturbation

backlog.spec: Set MAX_ITER to 100 for fresh random starts in the first 30% of the time, which gives about twice as many restarts. Re-run the best 2 of those with 400 iterations from their own end points. Then proceed with the perturbation phase from the best. Differs from earlier screening ideas because there is no threshold and no separate screen period.
backlog.title: Short-iteration restarts for the first phase

backlog.spec: Rerun the slot 29 scheme to confirm it. After 30% of the time on random restarts, in the perturbation phase, half the time remove the 3 smallest circles of the best packing and place them at random positions with radius 0.02. Set the other circles' radii to x0.5, then re-optimise with SLSQP. Otherwise use the existing jitter perturbation. Keep the best result.
backlog.title: Replicate slot 29 remove-and-reinsert

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, keep a current packing separate from the best. Each step perturbs the current packing (jitter sd 0.01-0.03, radii x0.5), re-optimises, and accepts it if its sum is >= current - 0.003. Otherwise revert to the current packing. Reset the current packing to the best every 8 failures. Update the best whenever the sum improves.
backlog.title: Chained perturbation with acceptance

backlog.spec: Set the restart phase to 20% of the time. In the perturbation phase, choose sd from [0.01, 0.02, 0.03, 0.05, 0.08] and radii scale from [0.3, 0.5, 0.7] at random each time. Perturb the best packing only.
backlog.title: Restart phase 20% with larger perturbation pool

backlog.spec: Reserve the last 8% of the time. Take the best packing and run SLSQP with ftol=1e-15 and maxiter=400 from its own centres and radii minus 1e-7. Use bounds r in [0, 0.5] and c in [0, 1]. Repair the result and keep it only if its sum is larger.
backlog.title: Final tight polish via bounded SLSQP

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts, first run 50 SLSQP iterations with the objective -sum(w_i r_i). Draw w_i from uniform(0.5, 1.5) per restart. Then run the normal 200-iteration SLSQP on the true objective from that point. This diversifies the basins reached.
backlog.title: Weighted objective warm start

backlog.spec: Keep the top 4 distinct packings from the restart phase. In the later phase, build a child by taking the circles of packing A with centre x < t (random t in 0.3-0.7) and the circles of packing B with x >= t. Fix the circle count to 26 by dropping the smallest circles or adding random ones at radius 0.02. Set radii x0.5 and re-optimise.
backlog.title: Region crossover of elite packings

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, half the time pick a random centre point and a radius of 0.25-0.4. Rotate the circles inside that disc about the point by a random angle of 20-90 degrees. Set radii x0.5 and re-optimise from the result. Otherwise use the existing jitter.
backlog.title: Block rotation perturbation

backlog.spec: After the main loop, which stops at 90% of the time, take the best packing. Run scipy trust-constr with the same inequality constraints, using a NonlinearConstraint with bounds [0, inf) and maxiter=300, from the best packing with radii minus 1e-6. Repair the result and keep it if the sum is larger.
backlog.title: Trust-constr final polish

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, first solve the problem with 25 circles using a short SLSQP of 100 iterations. Then add one circle at the point of largest clearance, with radius 0.02, and run the full SLSQP on 26 circles. Use this for half of the restarts.
backlog.title: Smaller-circle-count seeding

backlog.spec: In the restart phase, use MAX_ITER=80 for the first 15% of the time. Keep the best 3 packings. Then run a 300-iteration SLSQP continuation from each. After that, perturb the best as in slot 2 for the remaining time.
backlog.title: Short-iteration restart sweep

backlog.spec: For each fresh random restart, before SLSQP, run a few L-BFGS-B iterations minimising -sum(r) + mu * sum(max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij)^2) + wall penalties over (centres, radii) with mu increasing 10, 100, 1000 across three stages of 30 iterations each, using an analytic gradient via numpy. Then hand the result to SLSQP with MAX_ITER 150. Keeps the existing perturbation phase unchanged.
backlog.title: Penalty-free log-barrier warm start

backlog.spec: Set the restart phase to 25% of the time. Afterwards keep a current packing and a best packing. Each cycle perturbs the current one (radii x0.5, centre noise sd chosen from [0.01,0.02,0.04]), re-optimises with SLSQP, and accepts it as current if its sum is >= current sum - 0.002 (otherwise stays). Track best separately and return best.
backlog.title: Perturb phase: 25 percent restart, chained acceptance

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase always (not half the time) remove the 3 smallest circles of the best packing, place them at random points chosen as the farthest-from-existing-centres among 200 random candidates each, set all radii x0.5 (new circles radius 0.03), and re-optimise with SLSQP. Combine with slot 2's 30% restart phase.
backlog.title: Remove-3-smallest reinsert with tuned frequency 100 percent

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts, assign 4 to 6 circles an initial radius of 0.13 and the others 0.07 (random which), placing centres by sequential dart throwing with rejection so initial overlaps are small (up to 200 tries each, largest first). This mimics the known big/small structure of the best packings.
backlog.title: Two-radius-class starts

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP first with objective -sum(w_i r_i) where w_i are random weights uniform(0.7,1.3) for 80 iterations, then continue with the true objective for 200 iterations. Applies to fresh random restarts only.
backlog.title: Objective smoothing via radius-weight annealing

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts, sample 26 points, then do 5 Lloyd iterations using a 60x60 grid of the unit square (assign grid points to nearest centre, move centre to centroid of its cell) to get a well-spread configuration, add jitter sd 0.02, initial radii 0.05. Use this for all fresh restarts.
backlog.title: Lloyd-style centroidal start

backlog.spec: Replace the greedy repair with a vectorised loop: scale each overlapping pair's radii until max overlap <= 0, then use SHRINK=1e-12 rather than 1e-9, and verify validity with exact tolerance checks, shrinking all radii by 2e-12 more if any violation remains. Gains about 1e-9 each, so mostly tests safety; keep only if clean.
backlog.title: Final exact LP-free tightening of validity margin

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 30% switch with a bandit: each iteration chooses between a fresh restart and a perturbation of the best, with probability proportional to the (smoothed) count of past improvements per method, starting at 50/50 with prior 1 success each, with perturbation forced at least 50% after 20% of time.
backlog.title: Adaptive restart/perturb split by success rate

backlog.spec: After 30% of time, generate a batch of 4 perturbed children of the best (different sd), run each with MAX_ITER 60 only, then fully optimise (300 iterations) only the child with the highest intermediate sum. Repeat. This is a successive-halving selection inside the perturbation phase.
backlog.title: Batch-parallel-style population of perturbations

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, scale the best packing's centres about (0.5,0.5) by a factor from uniform(0.85,0.95), set radii to 0.5 times the original, add noise sd 0.01, and re-optimise with SLSQP. This creates compressed structures that relax into different arrangements, as a replacement for pure Gaussian jitter in half of the cycles.
backlog.title: Squeeze-and-expand wall perturbation

backlog.spec: After the main loop ends (stop it at 90% of TIME_FRACTION), take the best packing and run scipy trust-constr (or SLSQP with ftol=1e-15, maxiter 300) from it with the same constraints, accept only if the repaired sum improves. Repair afterwards as before. Use remaining time only; skip if less than 1.5 s remain.
backlog.title: Trust-constr free final polish

backlog.spec: Change SHRINK from 1e-9 to 2e-11 and in _repair run up to 200 iterations instead of 50, then do a final exact check: compute the max pair overlap and wall violation, and if any exceeds 1e-11 shrink all radii by that amount plus 1e-12. This recovers about 1e-8 per circle, tiny but free, and keeps validity under the 1e-10 tolerance.
backlog.title: Tighter repair shrink 1e-12

backlog.spec: Pass bounds to minimize: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]. Drop the explicit r>=0 constraints from cons (the bounds handle them) to cut the constraint count by 26 and the work per iteration. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Bounded SLSQP with box bounds

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts, run SLSQP first with objective -sum(w_i r_i) where w_i = 1 + 0.5*u_i, u_i uniform in [-1,1] per circle, for 50 iterations, then switch to the true objective for the full MAX_ITER. Weights are drawn from rng. This breaks symmetry between circles and encourages varied radius distributions.
backlog.title: Radius-weight annealed objective

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts, choose k uniformly from 4..8 circles as large with initial radius 0.14 and the other circles with initial radius 0.07, centres uniform in [0.1,0.9]. The best known packings have a mix of large and small circles, so this gives a start closer to that structure.
backlog.title: Two-radius-class starts

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts, draw 26 random points and do 5 Lloyd iterations on a 60x60 grid of sample points in the unit square (assign each sample to the nearest point, move the points to cluster means). Use the result as centres with initial radius 0.06. This gives well-spread starts without being a lattice.
backlog.title: Lloyd-relaxed centroidal starts

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, half the time scale the best packing's centres about (0.5,0.5) by a factor from uniform(0.85,0.95), radii x0.5, add noise sd 0.01, and re-optimise with SLSQP. This compresses the packing toward the centre so that the optimiser re-forms the wall contacts and finds different contact graphs. The other half uses the existing jitter.
backlog.title: Squeeze-and-expand wall perturbation

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 30% switch with an adaptive rule. Alternate between a fresh random restart and a perturbation of the best packing. Track the number of improvements from each type, and choose the next type with probability proportional to (successes+1)/(trials+2). Allow perturbations only after 10% of the time has elapsed.
backlog.title: Adaptive restart/perturb split

backlog.spec: Raise MAX_ITER to 600 for both fresh and perturbed solves, and also pass options ftol=1e-10 to SLSQP. Fresh starts are fewer but fully converged; keep the 30% restart / perturb split from slot 2. This tests whether under-converged runs are the bottleneck.
backlog.title: Larger iteration budget with fewer restarts

backlog.spec: After the main loop (stop it at 85% of the time limit), take the best packing and run scipy minimize with method='trust-constr' on the same objective and constraints (variables bounded to [0,1] for centres and [0,0.5] for radii), maxiter 300, starting from the best. Keep the result only if after _repair its sum of radii exceeds the best. Keep the existing repair step.
backlog.title: Trust-constr final polish

backlog.spec: Pass bounds to SLSQP: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5], and remove the radius>=0 constraint r from cons (keep the wall constraints). This shrinks the constraint vector and keeps the iterates in a sane region. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Bounded SLSQP with box bounds

backlog.spec: For fresh random restarts, choose k uniformly from 4..10 circles as 'large' with initial radius 0.14 and give the others initial radius 0.06. Centres are uniform in [0.1,0.9]. Large circles are placed first with a rejection sampling pass (up to 20 tries each) to keep them at least 0.2 apart. Everything else is unchanged.
backlog.title: Two-radius-class starts

backlog.spec: For fresh random restarts, draw 26 uniform points in the unit square, then run 8 Lloyd iterations using a 40x40 grid of sample points: assign each sample to its nearest point and move each point to the mean of its samples. Use the result as the initial centres, with radius 0.05. Keep the perturbation phase unchanged.
backlog.title: Lloyd-relaxed centroidal starts

backlog.spec: In _solve_once for fresh starts, run SLSQP in two stages. Stage 1 (60 iterations) minimises -sum(w*r) with w=1+0.5*(r_init-rank-based random values drawn from U(-1,1)) fixed per circle. Stage 2 (200 iterations) uses the plain objective starting from the stage 1 result. Apply it to half of the fresh restarts only.
backlog.title: Radius-weight annealed objective

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, with probability 0.5 build the start from the best packing by scaling all centres about (0.5,0.5) by a factor drawn from U(0.85,0.95), halving the radii and adding noise sd 0.01 to the centres. Otherwise use the existing perturbation. Re-optimise with SLSQP as before.
backlog.title: Squeeze-and-expand wall perturbation

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 30% switch to perturbation. After 15% of the time, track the improvements credited to each move type (fresh restart vs perturbation of the best). For each iteration choose perturbation with probability (p+1)/(p+f+2), where p is the number of perturbation successes (improved best) and f the number of fresh successes. Fresh restarts continue to be allowed throughout.
backlog.title: Adaptive restart/perturb split

backlog.spec: Set SHRINK to 1e-12, and in _repair after the loop run one final check with a vectorised exact pair test. If any pair still overlaps by more than 1e-12, scale the radii by 1-1e-10 and repeat up to 5 times. This keeps the gain of a smaller margin and still leaves the packing valid.
backlog.title: Tighter repair shrink

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, each round creates 4 perturbed copies of the best with different sd values (0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.04), runs SLSQP with MAX_ITER=100 on each, and fully polishes (200 more iterations) only the best-scoring one after repair. Accept it if it beats the best.
backlog.title: Population of perturbations, best of K

backlog.spec: For the first 20% of the time, solve n-1=25 circles with random restarts. Then for each of the top 3 solutions, insert a 26th circle at the largest empty hole (the point maximising the distance to the circles and the walls, found on a 50x50 grid), set its radius to 0.03 and the other radii x0.9, and run full SLSQP. Use the best result as the incumbent, and go on with the existing perturbation phase for the rest of the time.
backlog.title: Drop one circle and re-grow with 25-circle solutions

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts, run SLSQP in two stages. Stage 1 (60 iterations) uses the objective -sum(w_i*r_i) with w_i = 1 + 0.5*(r_i_start-mean) style fixed random weights drawn from U(0.5,1.5) per circle. Stage 2 (200 iterations) uses the true objective starting from the stage-1 solution. Time stays shared with the usual loop and only 50% of fresh starts use this.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius-weight annealing

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts, choose k uniformly from 4..8 large circles with initial radius 0.14 and the rest with initial radius 0.07. Place the large circles by rejection sampling at least 0.25 apart, the small ones uniformly in [0.05,0.95]. Run the normal SLSQP. Use this for all fresh starts.
backlog.title: Two-radius-class starts

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts, draw 26 uniform points, then run 10 Lloyd iterations on a 60x60 grid of sample points in the unit square (assign each sample to its nearest point, move each point to the centroid of its samples). Use the result as the centres with initial radius 0.06 and run SLSQP as before.
backlog.title: Lloyd-relaxed centroidal starts

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, each round create K=4 perturbed copies of the best packing with different sd values (0.005,0.01,0.02,0.04), and cheaply solve each with SLSQP limited to 60 iterations. Fully re-optimise (200 iterations) only the one with the largest radius sum. Update best if improved.
backlog.title: Population of K perturbations, best of K

backlog.spec: Take the best packing, delete a random circle (preferring the smallest 5), and re-solve SLSQP with n=25 for 100 iterations. Then insert a new circle with a small initial radius 0.02 at the point of greatest clearance, found over a 100x100 grid as the distance to nearest circle edge and walls. Re-optimise all 26 with SLSQP for 200 iterations. Run this in the perturbation phase half the time, in place of the x0.5 perturbation.
backlog.title: Drop-one and regrow from 25-circle solution

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 30% switch. Start with restarts only. After 15% of the time, run perturbation rounds, tracking the number of improvements from perturbation. If no perturbation improved the best in the last 8 attempts, do one fresh restart. Always run perturbation in the last 40% of the time.
backlog.title: Adaptive restart-vs-perturb split by success

backlog.spec: Pass options eps=1e-8 (finite-difference step, default is about 1.5e-8) and ftol=1e-9 to the SLSQP call. Keep the rest of the solver unchanged, including the constraint form. This is a pure solver-numerics change that may change the convergence quality at the same iteration count.
backlog.title: Bounded SLSQP with SLSQP eps tuning

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts, put 4 circles with initial radius 0.12 near the four corners (centres at 0.12 from both walls plus noise sd 0.01). Place the remaining 22 uniformly in [0.1,0.9] with initial radius 0.05. Run the normal SLSQP. Use this for half the fresh restarts and keep the rest as is.
backlog.title: Corner-pair anchored starts

backlog.spec: Replace the greedy pairwise _repair with: clip centres into [0,1], compute for fixed centres the optimal radii by scipy.optimize.linprog (maximise sum r subject to r_i+r_j <= d_ij, r_i <= wall distance_i, r>=0), then subtract 1e-12 from every radius and clamp at 0. Run it only once on the final best packing and also on each candidate to compare sums. Keep the old repair as fallback if linprog fails. Goal: remove greedy shrink losses and the 1e-9 margin.
backlog.title: Final exact-feasibility repair via LP with margin

backlog.spec: After the restart/perturb loop ends at 85% of time, take the best packing and run one SLSQP using only pair constraints whose distance minus radii sum is below 0.02 (plus all wall constraints), with ftol=1e-15 and maxiter 500, starting from the packing with radii unchanged. Accept only if the repaired result has a larger sum. Reserve 10% of the time limit for this.
backlog.title: Tight-SLSQP polish with active-set constraint set

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts, replace the SLSQP start by an inflation scheme: all radii equal to a common scale s, centres optimised by L-BFGS-B on the sum of squared overlaps plus wall violations, with s raised in 6 steps from 0.06 to 0.11 (warm start each step). Then use the resulting centres with radii 0.9 of the feasible values as the SLSQP start. Use the seed rng for the initial centres.
backlog.title: Smooth penalty objective with growing radii (inflation schedule)

backlog.spec: Set the switch from fresh restarts to perturbation at 15% of the time limit instead of 30%, and use MAX_ITER=120 for perturbation solves (which start near an optimum) while keeping 200 for fresh starts. This yields more perturbation cycles from a good basin.
backlog.title: Tune restart fraction and iteration cap together

backlog.spec: In _solve_once for fresh starts, first solve with objective -sum(r_i^p) with p=0.5 (favours equalising radii) for 60 iterations, then continue with the true objective -sum(r) for 200 iterations starting from that solution. Use the same constraints. Different from random per-circle weights: it is a deterministic concave power transform.
backlog.title: Variable-radius-weight objective annealing

backlog.spec: For half of fresh starts, place 16 circles evenly around a ring near the walls (perimeter spacing with a small random jitter and radius 0.09 at distance 0.09 from the walls) and the other 10 circles at random positions in [0.25,0.75]^2 with radius 0.1. The known good packings have a boundary ring of larger-spaced circles with an interior cluster, so this biases toward them. The rest use uniform starts.
backlog.title: Boundary-ring plus interior structured starts

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, take the best packing, add a 27th circle at the biggest hole (the sampled point with max distance clearance), run SLSQP for 27 circles for 100 iterations, then delete the circle with the smallest radius and run the 26-circle SLSQP polish for 200 iterations. Accept if the repaired sum improves.
backlog.title: Remove-worst-and-resolve with 27 circles then delete

backlog.spec: Scale the SLSQP variables so that centres and radii have comparable magnitude: optimise over y=v/0.1 (i.e. the constraint and objective use 0.1*y) so SLSQP's finite-difference steps (eps default 1.5e-8) and tolerances act relatively. Also set options eps=1e-9. Keep everything else the same and the repair step unchanged.
backlog.title: Radius-ordered symmetry-breaking constraints removal via variable scaling

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase use a sd that cycles geometrically through 0.08, 0.04, 0.02, 0.01, 0.005 over consecutive perturbation attempts, restarting at 0.08 after a full cycle with no improvement of the best. Always perturb the best packing with radii x0.5 as in the accepted slot 2. If 8 attempts in a row fail to improve, do one fresh random restart instead and keep it only if better than best.
backlog.title: Annealed perturbation size with restart-on-stagnation

backlog.spec: Revert to the slot-2 configuration exactly (restart 30% of the time, then perturb the best with radii x0.5 and sd from [0.005,0.01,0.02,0.05]). Make no other change. This gives a replicate to measure the true incumbent level against noise sd 0.0023, so later decisions are not made against a lucky -2.6349.
backlog.title: Replicate slot 2 baseline unchanged

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, take the best packing, remove the 3 smallest circles, and place them at random points drawn from the 10 largest-clearance candidates among 2000 random samples (clearance = distance to nearest remaining centre minus its radius, and distance to walls). Give them radius 0.03, jitter all centres with sd 0.01, scale radii x0.5, and re-optimise with SLSQP. Alternate with the slot-2 perturbation 50/50. It differs from slot 29 in using the top-10 candidates and the extra jitter.
backlog.title: Remove 3 smallest and reinsert, 100% of perturbations plus sd jitter

backlog.spec: Make the final SLSQP solution more feasible so repair loses less: after each solve, run one more SLSQP call of at most 30 iterations with ftol=1e-15 starting from the result, with constraints shifted by a margin of 1e-11 (cons(v) - 1e-11). Then call _repair. Set SHRINK=1e-12. This reduces the loss from repair and reduces the slack left at the end.
backlog.title: Cheap greedy repair replaced by LP-free multiplicative scaling inside SLSQP end

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, each round creates K=4 perturbed children of the current best with different sd values from [0.005,0.01,0.02,0.04] and runs SLSQP with MAX_ITER=100 on each. Then run a full 200-iteration SLSQP only on the best child, and replace the best if it improves. This uses a cheap screen to select perturbations.
backlog.title: Population of K perturbations, keep best

backlog.spec: For fresh random restarts, draw 26 random points, then run 10 Lloyd iterations (using a 64x64 grid of sample points, assign each to its nearest centre, move the centres to the cell centroids). Use the result as centres with initial radius 0.06 (about half the nearest-neighbour distance). This gives starts that are evenly spread and not clumped.
backlog.title: Lloyd-relaxed centroidal starts

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, run SLSQP in two stages. Stage 1 (60 iterations) maximises sum(r_i^0.5) which favours equal radii. Stage 2 (200 iterations) maximises sum(r). Use the same constraints. Take the stage 1 result as the start for stage 2 without shrinking radii.
backlog.title: Radius-weight annealed objective

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, use sd that starts at 0.05 and is multiplied by 0.8 on each failure to improve the best, reset to 0.05 after sd drops below 0.004. If 15 consecutive failures occur, discard the best-so-far for perturbation purposes and run one fresh random restart as the new perturbation base (still keep the global best for return).
backlog.title: Adaptive annealed perturbation size with stagnation restarts

backlog.spec: Spend 15% of the time solving 27-circle problems with random starts (n+1 circles). Then for the best 27 packing, delete each of the 27 circles in turn, giving 26-circle starts, re-optimise each with SLSQP (radii x0.9), and keep the best. After that, use the normal slot-2 perturbation of the best until the time runs out. The rest of the time uses the usual restarts.
backlog.title: Drop-one regrow from 27 circles

backlog.spec: Pass bounds to SLSQP (centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]) and drop the r>=0 and some wall constraints into bounds, and set options eps=1e-9 (finite-difference step) rather than the default 1.5e-8. Check that the finite-difference accuracy is better, so convergence in 200 iterations improves. Keep everything else as in slot 2.
backlog.title: Bounded variables with SLSQP eps tuning

backlog.spec: Half of fresh restarts: put k random between 14 and 18 circles evenly spaced on a ring inset 0.08 from the square boundary (with a random angular offset and small noise sd 0.01), and put the remaining circles at random positions in [0.25,0.75]^2. Initial radius 0.06 for the ring and 0.08 for the interior. The other half stay uniform random.
backlog.title: Boundary-ring plus interior structured starts

backlog.spec: Make the single change that slot 2 made, which is the current incumbent: after 30% of the time on random restarts, perturb the best packing (radii x0.5, centre noise sd chosen from [0.005,0.01,0.02,0.05]) and re-optimise. Change nothing else. This measures the true level of the incumbent against the noise (sd 0.0023), so later decisions have a reliable baseline.
backlog.title: Replicate slot 2 baseline unchanged

backlog.spec: After the main loop, take the best packing. Fix the centres and compute the maximum-sum radii with scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS). The constraints are r_i + r_j <= d_ij - 1e-12 and r_i <= wall distance - 1e-12, with r >= 0. Use the result only if the sum is larger than the repaired best, and verify validity exactly before returning. This replaces the greedy repair loss only at the end, not inside the loop.
backlog.title: Slack-variable free LP-like final tightening

backlog.spec: After 30% of the time, each round creates K=4 perturbed copies of the best packing (radii x0.5, sd from the existing list). Run SLSQP with MAX_ITER=100 on each. Then re-run the top-1 for the full 200 iterations. Update best if it improves. This is a successive-halving selection among perturbations, so fewer full solves are wasted on bad ones.
backlog.title: Parallel-free population: best of K perturbations per round

backlog.spec: Change the SLSQP variables from r to s = r / 0.1 (scaled by 10) and the centres to c*10. Divide constraints accordingly so all variables are O(1) to O(10). Keep the constraint function equivalent in the scaled units. The aim is better conditioning of SLSQP's BFGS, so it converges to better optima in 200 iterations.
backlog.title: Optimise in log-radius parameterisation with per-circle scaling

backlog.spec: For half of the fresh restarts, optimise 13 circles (centre c, radius r) together with their images under the point reflection (1-c) about (0.5,0.5), giving 26 circles. Run SLSQP on the 13-circle variables with constraints between all 26 circles. Then release the symmetry: run the usual 200 iterations on the full 26 circles from that solution. Many strong packings are near-symmetric, and this halves the search dimension.
backlog.title: Symmetry-tied 13+13 central-inversion packing

backlog.spec: Reserve the last 10% of the time. Run scipy trust-constr (with a sparse or finite-difference Jacobian) from the best packing using the same constraints, with xtol=1e-12 and maxiter limited by the remaining time. Use the result only if it is valid after the existing repair and has a larger sum. The goal is to reach a tighter local optimum than SLSQP's 200 iterations.
backlog.title: Interior-point trust-constr full polish only on the final 10%

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, draw 26 random points and relax them with 100 steps of gradient descent on the energy sum 1/d^2 over pairs plus wall repulsion 1/(2*wall distance)^2. Use a small random multiplicative jitter of 5%. Set the initial radii to 0.4 times the nearest-neighbour distance, capped by wall distance. Then run SLSQP as usual. This gives evenly spread starts that differ from the Lloyd, hex and grid starts tried so far, because they come from a physical relaxation.
backlog.title: Repulsion-energy initialisation (Riesz) with size gradient

backlog.spec: Set SHRINK to 1e-11. After repair, run a quick exact check with the harness tolerance of 1e-10: compute the max overlap and wall violation in double precision, and if it is below 1e-12 keep the radii. Also stop the loop at TIME_FRACTION 0.85 with a check on the per-restart time. This recovers about 1e-9 per circle, which is tiny, but it costs one line.
backlog.title: Lower the repair shrink and reduce time waste

backlog.spec: In fresh restarts, add a quadratic penalty mu*sum(max(0, 0.04 - r_i)^2) to the SLSQP objective for the first 80 iterations (mu=5). Then drop it and continue for 200 iterations. This discourages tiny circles early on, so the optimiser must place all 26 as useful discs before the sum is maximised. It is a regularisation rather than a start-distribution change.
backlog.title: Radius-ordered ghost constraints: soft penalty on the smallest circle

backlog.spec: Keep a list of the top 8 packings from the restart phase, with their sums. In the perturbation phase, pick the parent by rank-weighted sampling (weights 1/rank), not always the best. Apply the radii x0.5 plus sd noise perturbation, re-optimise, and insert the child into the list if it beats the worst and is distinct (sum differs by more than 1e-6). This lets the search spread across several basins, unlike the earlier always-best perturbation.
backlog.title: Tabu perturbation: re-optimise from a different elite packing each round

backlog.spec: Make no change to train.py (keep the current 30% restart then radii x0.5 perturbation scheme) and run it again, to measure the true incumbent level under noise sd 0.0023. Use this value as the baseline for later comparisons.
backlog.title: Replicate incumbent unchanged

backlog.spec: Optimise only 13 circles (26 centre coordinates plus 13 radii) and build the other 13 as point reflections through (0.5,0.5): centre (1-x,1-y), same radius. Write the SLSQP constraints on the full 26-circle set built from these variables, with random starts. Use this for the first 30% of the time to get good seeds. Then switch to the existing unconstrained perturbation phase, starting from the best symmetric packing as best.
backlog.title: Central-inversion symmetric 13+13 packing

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, first solve a smoothed problem with SLSQP: the objective is -sum(r) and every pair constraint is d_ij >= r_i+r_j+m, with margin m=0.01. Then re-solve with m=0 from that solution. The margin makes the first solve find well-spread configurations. Compare it against the current single solve. Keep the rest of the script unchanged.
backlog.title: Log-sum-exp smooth max-radius barrier continuation

backlog.spec: In the restart phase, start 12 random 60-iteration SLSQP runs, keep the best 4, continue each of these from its own x for 100 more iterations (warm start the SLSQP with the x it returned), keep the best 1 and run it to 300 iterations. Repeat this tournament until 30% of the time is used. After that, use the existing perturbation phase on the best result.
backlog.title: Time-sliced successive halving of restarts

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, instead of scaling all radii by 0.5, take the best packing, set the 5 smallest circles' radii to 0 and all other radii to 0.9 times their value, and add centre noise sd 0.01. Then run SLSQP. The small circles can regrow wherever there is room, and the larger ones keep their structure. Use this in half of the perturbation steps.
backlog.title: Perturbation by radius-ordered inflation of the smallest circles

backlog.spec: Pass options eps=1e-7 to SLSQP (the default is about 1.5e-8). The coarser step may give more stable steps with the noisy sqrt distance constraints, and it may converge in fewer iterations. Keep everything else the same. If it is neutral, also try eps=1e-6.
backlog.title: Use SLSQP eps tuning for the finite-difference Jacobian

backlog.spec: Spend 15% of the time optimising 28 circles. Then remove the 2 circles with the smallest radii, re-optimise the 26 that remain with SLSQP, and keep the best. Afterwards, the existing perturbation phase works on this best packing. The extra circles move the structure into denser arrangements.
backlog.title: Larger count then prune: 28 circles to 26

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform starts with a short Metropolis simulated-annealing run on the centres, with the 26 radii given by a one-step LP or the min-distance rule, for example r_i = 0.5*min(nearest neighbour distance, 2*wall distance). Run 300 single-circle moves with step sd 0.05 that decays, and accept a move if sum(r) goes up or with exp(delta/T) for T=0.01 decaying to 0. Use the result as the SLSQP start.
backlog.title: Pair-penalty repulsion with annealed temperature starts

backlog.spec: For the last 20% of the time, run only small perturbations of the best packing (centre sd 0.002 to 0.008, radii x0.95) and run SLSQP at MAX_ITER=100, accepting the child if its repaired sum improves. This is a fine local search around the best optimum. Keep the first 80% unchanged: 30% fresh restarts, then the perturbation phase.
backlog.title: Final best-of-all polishing with random small-sd restarts

backlog.spec: Replace the greedy pair-shrink _repair loop. Compute r = min(r, wall distance), then repeatedly scale r_i, r_j for the worst overlapping pair down with the existing code, but afterwards take a final pass that computes the largest radius for each circle in turn (r_i = min(wall dist, min_j(d_ij - r_j)) - 1e-12) in order of increasing radius, so that no valid slack is lost. Set SHRINK to 1e-12. Check that the result is still valid under the tolerance of 1e-10.
backlog.title: Slack-free exact repair via scaling

incumbent.description: After 30% of the time on random restarts, perturb the best packing (radii x0.5, centre noise sd drawn from {0.005,0.01,0.02,0.05}) and re-run SLSQP, keeping improvements.

memo: Helped: only slot 2 (30% of time on random restarts, then perturb the best packing with radii x0.5 and re-optimise), -2.6349 from one run. Slots 6, 7, 16, 18 and 27 reached -2.6354, and slots 29 and 68 gave the best raw value, -2.6360. All are within noise (sd 0.0023) of slot 2, so none is confirmed. Did not help: start-distribution changes (wall-biased, Latin hypercube, mirrored, hex rows, two radius classes), solver changes (analytic Jacobians, pruning, box bounds, MAX_ITER 1000 gave -2.6284), screen-then-polish, LP radii, swaps, basin hopping, crossover, rotate/translate (-2.6275), chained perturbation (-2.6272, -2.6314), final polish. Many ideas were aborted as duplicates. Next: replicate slots 2, 29 and 68 to confirm the -2.635 level. Then tune restart fraction (20% vs 50%) and perturbation size. Then combine slot 29 with slot 6 or 7 starts. Avoid already-tried ideas.
